newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA NEW VEHICLE SALES UP 7-MTHS TO JULY.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA NEW VEHICLE SALES UP 7-MTHS TO JULY.

text.p: Australian new motor vehicle sales fell 15.5 percent in July from June but remained 6.9 percent ahead for the year to date, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said on Thursday.
The FCAI said its forecast for full year sales was unchanged at 660,000 vehicles compared with 610,000 in 1996.
The industry body said July total sales of 59,741 were up 11.3 percent from a year earlier.
The FCAI said the passenger vehicle sales rose by 4,040 in July from June and were up 9.7 percent from July 1996.
In year-to-date terms, passenger vehicle sales rose 5.3 percent due to continued strength in the small car segment where sales were running 24.5 percent ahead of 1996, the FCAI said.
Sports car and luxury car sales were up 41.7 percent and 26.9 percent respectively in the seven months to July.

Light truck sales were 12.6 percent higher in year-to-date terms, reflecting strong sales in the four wheel drive sector, while heavy truck sales were up five percent against the first seven months of 1996.
Ford Motor Co held the top sales position in July with 18.6 percent market share (18.7 percent year to date).
General Motors Corp had a 16.4 percent market share in July (16.8 percent year to date) while Toyota Motor Corp held a 15.8 percent in July (17.0 percent year to date).
